entities.summary:
Acharya Jinasena (unknown - 838 CE) was a prominent Digambar Jain monk, scholar, and religious leader in 8th-century India.

He is widely known for composing the Adipurana and Mahapurana, considered the foundational texts of Jain Sanskrit literature, and for serving as the royal spiritual advisor to the Rashtrakuta emperor Amoghavarsha. He also finished the Jaidhavala commentary started by his guru Virasena.

Jinasena played a pivotal role in shaping Jain philosophy and spirituality during this period, and his works continue to be studied and revered by scholars and practitioners of Jainism today.

The significance of Jinasena's contributions lies in their impact on the development of Jain literature and the spread of Jainism throughout India and beyond.
